The tree was empty and there are no results yet, so I seeded it with 4 Lvl1 hypotheses on different directions. Each has Lvl2 mechanisms and Lvl3 predictions with numeric thresholds. - **H1, epochs to target:** the main lever is cutting the number of epochs needed for 75%. Mechanisms:   - an airbench96-style backbone with whitening and Dirac init;   - Muon for the conv filters;   - label smoothing 0.3 plus Lookahead/EMA;   - alternating flip, which should matter more because test-time augmentation is banned. - **H2, cost per epoch:**   - keep data on the GPU and augment there, which matters a lot with only 4 CPU cores;   - a vectorised optimizer, compiled step, fp16 with channels_last, and CUDA graphs;   - progressive resizing 24→28→32 px;   - hard-example filtering with a proxy model (low prior). - **H3, fixed timed overhead:**   - compile or autotune leaking out of build when a shape wasn't warmed up;   - the cost of prepare() itself. - **H4, accuracy margin:**   - seed and time noise; a 3-seed mean below about 0.756 is fragile for the 40-seed judgment;   - near 9 epochs, epoch count trades smoothly against margin. Suggested order of experiments: 1. Run the unmodified template twice to measure noise (H4.1.1). 2. Test GPU-resident data on the template (H2.1.1), so data-pipeline gains aren't mixed up with architecture changes. 3. Port the airbench96-style net at 9 epochs with LS 0.3 (H1.1.1). The PR's reference to beat is about 8.1 s, but at 75.29% it is below our 0.753 bar. 4. Only then try Muon, progressive resizing and systems work, one change per run. Every run needs a compliance check: eval timed at B = 1, 7, 512 and 1024, no real data used in build, and every training shape warmed up in build. Treat time differences under about 2× the measured noise as inconclusive, since the judging card is an A100 PCIe rather than the SXM4 used here.

Changes to the tree: **Closed or changed by evidence** - **H1.1.1 refuted (E001).** The 9-epoch run reached 0.7430, below the pre-registered 0.745 threshold. - **Compile speedup supported (E004).**   - H2.2.1 gets E004+, which overrides E003~: −14% time with bit-identical accuracy.   - H2.2 is marked supported, and H2's confidence goes up. - **H3.1 supported and reworded (E003).** It now covers stride, layout, dtype and requires_grad guards, not only shapes. This explains the E003 counterexample: warm-up used NCHW tensors while training used channels_last, so a ~9 s recompile happened inside the timed region. - **H3.2 refuted.** Measured prepare is 0.06–0.21 s, about 1–2% of a trial.   - H3.2.1 and H3.1.1 are retired.   - H3 is lowered to 0.2 and reworded to the only place left for fixed cost: one-time costs inside train(). - **Lookahead/EMA result (E005).**   - H1.3 and H1.3.2 are supported: +0.97 pp, every seed moved the same way.   - H1.3.2 drops the "9 epochs fixed" premise. E005 most likely ran at 10 epochs on the E004 base.   - H1 and H1.1 are supported: about 6.5x faster than the ResNet9 baseline. - **H4.2.1 token changed to E002~.** E002 tested 9→10 epochs, not 8.5→9. Excluding E001's seed-1 outlier, the gain is only about 0.28 pp. - **H2.1 and H2.1.1 retired.** The GPU data pipeline was bundled into E001 and cannot be tested in isolation. **Lowered by search** - H1.2 (Muon) goes to 0.25. The PR #3 precedent on this benchmark reports that Muon lost to SGD. - H2.4 (proxy data filtering) goes to 0.2. Its only evidence is a 45-epoch, 96% CIFAR-10 regime. - H2.2.2 (CUDA graphs) goes to 0.3. Fable found the training was not launch-bound. **H2.3 (progressive resizing)** All four committee members expect it to fail, but search shows about 10% savings on CIFAR-10. I reworded H2.3.1 into a decisive test: global max-pool head, each resolution compiled with static shapes and channels_last warm-up, and an explicit no-recompile guard. **Noise model (H4.1)** Compiled runs are deterministic per seed, so re-running a recipe measures no accuracy noise. Mean differences under about 0.3 pp are treated as noise. H1.3.1's threshold is raised to 0.3 pp to match. **New hypotheses** - **Why E005 worked (the second counterexample).** Four tests that separate the possible mechanisms:   - N1: decaying LR to 0 without EMA.   - N2: EMA plus decay to 0.   - N3: plain end-of-run EMA without Lookahead resets.   - N4: BatchNorm statistic recalibration after averaging. - **N5: CIFAR-10 settings may not suit CIFAR-100.** Children: N5a (lr×wd grid) and N5b (width 576→512). - **N6:** the epoch-trim slope measured on the EMA recipe, which is what the next epoch cuts depend on. - **N7:** an offline check on held-out seeds 3–12 for the 40-seed margin. - **N8:** graph breaks in the compiled train step. - **N9 and N9a:** first-epoch overhead inside train. **Suggested next steps** 1. Read E005's actual epoch count from its commit. 2. N1/N2: LR decay to 0. These are cheap and may add margin. 3. N6: trim epochs from E005. 4. N5b and H2.3.1 to cut per-epoch cost, using the TORCH_LOGS=recompiles check before each run.
